Melchoir the Precept: Ascended Druid, Centaur:

Melchoir grew up in Gildenburg, a small outpost town turned sprawling city near the Sinjin Dessert. The environment was brutal, with border scavengers and cartels raiding and causing carnage and death. Death was a daily occurrence, a fact of life - and in the face of this death and suffering, Melchoir grew great empathy for those trapped in the predicament around him. He survived by luck alone 'til the age of 13. One day, while combing the dessert collar for remnants of scavenger attacks, he came upon a particularly grisly scene.

A lone wagon had been set upon by a gang of mauraders, left burning with bodies strewn about. As he topped a knoll, Melchoir was able to see the gang riding off into the distance with cargo in tow, including a female who had been strung up behind a horse.

Pausing momentarily to ensure that the band of mauraders was out of sight, Melchoir beset upon the ravaged wagon. The bodies were badly impaled and disemboweled. No signs of life, not even a twitch. The travelers were all adorned in long, plain robes, common to any traveler of the harsh conditions the dessert would subject you to, but the method of murder was more barbaric then the usual heists are. Mostly scavengers and marauders alike would prefer to save the scarce ammunition they have in the remote regions of Gildenburg and the Sinjin dessert collar, often times victims run into the wild without chase as their belongings are ransacked.

Risking a glance in the burning wagon turned up no valueables, however outback of the wagon Melchoir found chest overturned, with a burning mound of scrolls and books piled up beside it in. Melchoir kicked at the pile of books, scattering the fire about in an attempt to salvage anything he could sell back in town. Only two items could be salvaged from the smoldering flames, two books, completely undamaged with no signs of burning.

It was this moment that the course Melchoir's life would change, forever, as he opened the books to reveal esoteric tomes from the Highest Druids of Temple Wohram. Melchoir could not make out the Druidic writings, and thumbed through the pages quickly trying to determine the nature of the books. He came to a page filled with many small sentences, written in many different languages. One of the languages was an old Elvish language Melchoir was exposed to as a child. The basic elvish words he could read, but the sentence didn't make any sense. The pages glowed with a dim blue light as he slowly uttered the Elvish words he could recall from the first line, "Make it true, who are you."

The Druidic Tome illuminated in a swirling green essence, rising up from it's pages and scattering 50 paces in each direction. A ringing sound alerted Melchoir to one of the bodies lying on the ground behind him, a green glow now emanating from one of his sleeves. Melchoir turned the corpse over, a man whose years were told by the length of his white beard, now turned crimson by his own blood - a horrified expression left with a blank stare adorned his face, mouth agape. Twisting the arm of the lifeless body, Melchoir works the hand from out of a bundle of excess fabric in the robe's sleeve and finds it clutching some sort of amulet.

The long, delicately crafted silvery chain and pendant shone brightly, almost glowing pure white beside the dazzling green gem set within it - emanating a visible, powerful green aura despite still being clutched within the death grip of the old man.

Suddenly, the dead man's hand opens. Gently, slowly. Almost offering the amulet to Melchoir as a gift.

"What gold could I bring for this?" Thought Melchoir as his eyes grew ever wider.

In shock, Melchoir's eyes shot back to the face of the corpse, now staring him dead in the eyes. The previous expression now solemn, stern even as the eyes appeared to challenge Melchoir - the previous gaping mouth was closed, poised, ready to give command, as the eyes of the dead pierced into the depths of his soul.

Melchoir moved to grab the amulet, and upon touching it was blinded by a swirling cosmic light. He could not feel anything, as if his body had been removed from him. A sensation of falling ten thousand miles in an instant followed by a spike of cosmic light being driven into Melchoir's third eye rends him on his back, next to the burning wagon. Smoke flies upwards, melding with the clouds stained pink from the sun's setting as Melchoir's blurry scene comes into focus.

He looks down to read the covers, "Druidity XII - Intermediate Spells, Sapping, & Summons, Druidity XCIX - Life and Death, Elder's Edition.

"We will be with you, Melchoir." The spirits warned as they faded into nothingness.
